summary.title: Effective learning: Twenty rules of formulating knowledge
summary.one_liner: Learn how to reformulate study material into simple, specific question-and-answer items (cloze deletions, split sets and enumerations) so spaced repetition becomes faster and more reliable.
takeaways: Understand material and build an overall picture before memorizing individual facts.
Keep each flashcard item minimal: short questions with short answers, following the minimum information principle.
Convert complex items into cloze deletions, and convert sets into ordered enumerations or grouped questions.
Use imagery, graphic deletion (occlusion) and mnemonics where the cost is justified.
Split enumerations such as the alphabet or poems into overlapping cloze items.
summary.summary: Piotr Wozniak's article presents 20 ordered rules for turning study material into items that suit spaced repetition in SuperMemo. It argues that simple, specific questions are learned faster and retained longer than dense textbook passages. Each rule is illustrated with before-and-after examples, such as the Dead Sea facts, a Kaleida company passage, and European Union membership. The page also includes SuperMemo-specific steps for creating cloze and graphic deletions in several versions of the software.
